title: Client pulse — Parkbench quickscan & request catalog
content:
Parkbench quickscan — high-level intent:

Purpose: rapid synthesis of customer signals collected during the late-May -> mid-June outreach run. Build a compact, prioritized catalog of concrete asks and friction spots that can be turned into 1–3 microprobes for the July sprint. Focus is on production-inference ergonomics (latency, model-fallthroughs, routing) and cost/leakage patterns.

Method / data sources:
- Intake windows: support tickets (Tier 2 escalation stream), two customer interviews (FinTech X & Healthcare Y), usage logs (top 50 tenants by token spend), and a 3-day lab replay of anomalous latency traces.
- Lightweight tagging: each signal annotated with impact-est (low/med/high), effort-est (S/M/L), and whether it is product, docs, or infra.
- Quick validation: pinged owning AE/SE for top-6 asks to confirm pain description.

Executive signal summary (what keeps recurring):
1) Latency tails on longer sequences (customer stories: multi-paragraph summarization jobs taking 2–3x expected time during bursts). Impact: High for batch customers; SLO slippage reported by 3 accounts.
2) Model substitution transparency — customers want deterministic fallback behavior when a preferred variant is unavailable (e.g., v1-quantized -> v1-float). Impact: Medium but high trust risk.
3) Billing surprises when caching triggers partial token credits (confusion over prefix cache vs fresh call). Impact: Medium; several small customers escalated.
4) Private deployment onboarding tempo — CLI & network checks brittle, early steps block for infra teams in regulated orgs. Impact: High for closed deals.
5) Observability surface gaps — customers want per-model request tagging and per-route token breakout in a single trace view. Impact: High for platform teams.

Parkbench request catalog (compact, prioritized):
- R1: Latency-tail mitigation quickpatch (canary autoscaler tweak + profile-guided batching). Impact: High; Effort: M. Proposed probe: enable burst-aware autoscaler and run 2-week A/B against 10 tenants. Owner: eng-sre + serving-runtime. Linked: JIRA CS-4217.
- R2: Deterministic fallback governance (API flag + console note + SDK default). Impact: Medium; Effort: S. Probe: add ?fallback=failover_variant param and show explicit logs in console for 1 month. Owner: product-hosted-api + devexp.
- R3: Billing transparency doc + sample invoice diff (short-term) + UX label change (long-term). Impact: Medium; Effort: S. Probe: publish one-pager and email to affected customers. Owner: finance-and-legal + customer-success.
- R4: Private onboarding CLI checklist and network preflight tool. Impact: High; Effort: M. Probe: ship a simplified binary that runs common checks (endpoint reach, KMS access test, port sanity). Owner: private-deployments + infra.
- R5: Per-route trace enrichment (token-by-route visualization). Impact: High; Effort: L. Probe: instrument 2 routes for 3 customers and capture token breakdown. Owner: observability + console-and-tooling.

Microprobe playbook (how to run the probes in 2 weeks):
1) Pick 2 probes (R1, R3) for immediate sprint. Keep R2 as a 1-week dev spike.
2) Define measurable success metrics (R1: 95th pct latency reduction; R3: #billing escalations drop to zero for affected cohort).
3) Lightweight rollout cadence: internal canary -> opt-in customer cohort -> auto-enroll.
4) Communication: status note in Support Channel and weekly Parkbench thread.

Risk flags and open questions (notes to self):
- R1: Autoscaler changes might increase cost if batching isn't properly gated — need a cost guardrail metric.
- R2: SDK default change could break existing customer integrations; require migration window.
- R4: Private onboarding tool could surface sensitive checks; clearance needed from security before shipping to customers.

Quantitative snapshots included in intake (high level):
- Top 50 tenants accounted for ~78% of burst incidents in May.
- Median token/session for flagged jobs: 1.8k tokens; 95th: 6.1k tokens.
- Billing confusion cluster accounts for 12% of small-tenant support tickets last quarter.

Customer quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "When the model switches mid-stream we lose context and our app retries cause doubled cost." — FinTech X (AE: Mariah).
- "Private install felt like a scavenger hunt — we got stuck waiting on a port we never knew to open." — Health Y (SE: Omar).

Suggested prioritization rationale (simple):
- Urgent & high-impact: R1, R4 (direct revenue/retention risk).
- Medium: R2, R3 (trust & support load).
- Lower immediate ROI but product-defining: R5 (observability; heavy lift).

Next actions (owner + eta):
- Aisha: prepare R1 canary run README + measurement plan by 2026-07-05.
- Diego: spike fallback flag implementation and safety checks by 2026-07-07.
- Priya: draft billing one-pager and coordinate with finance by 2026-07-06.
- Samira: coordinate private-onboard preflight spec and security review request by 2026-07-09.

Appendix — short experiment templates (copyable):
- A/B latency patch template: define cohort (10 tenants), baseline window (2 weeks), metric (95th pct latency), control vs variant notes, rollback criteria.
- Billing clarity doc skeleton: example invoice before/after, FAQ, one-line summary for console.

Unresolved items / parking lot:
- Should fallback behavior be opt-in or opt-out for hosted API? (ops vs trust tradeoff).
- Is there a meaningful quick observability surface we can ship without a console redesign?

Meeting logs + related links:
- Support thread: slack://CS/support-thread-parkbench
- Interview notes: confluence://parkbench/interviews-2026-05

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep probes tiny and measurable; avoid full-specification launches here.
- Use the Parkbench codename in internal comms to group these rapid experiments.
- Make sure finance sanity-checks any autoscaler changes before wide rollouts.

-- end of quickscan (Parkbench) — A.P.
